# Running the lab {#sec-running}

The lab lives in the repository [deburky/postgres-lab](https://github.com/deburky/postgres-lab) and
needs Docker.

## First run

```bash
git clone https://github.com/deburky/postgres-lab && cd postgres-lab
cp .env.example .env     # app / pwd / app on localhost:5432
uv sync
just db                  # Postgres 16 + pgvector + pgvectorscale
just smoke               # insert three documents, search them by cosine distance
```

`just` lists every recipe, and each recipe loads `.env`. For VS Code, the
repository includes a [dev container](https://github.com/deburky/postgres-lab/tree/main/.devcontainer)
with the database running next to it.

## The servers

| server | start | port | for |
|---|---|---|---|
| pg16 | `just db` | 5432 | most chapters |
| pg18 | `just db pg18` | 5441 | PRISM, pgmq, pgsesame |
| replica | `just db replica` | 5440 | logical replication |
| PgBouncer | `docker compose -f docker/pgbouncer.yaml up -d` | 6432 | PgBouncer |
| Doris | `just db doris` | 9030 | Doris CDC |
| ducklake | `just db ducklake` | 5443 | pg_ducklake |
| kind, k3d, k3s | `just k8s-up <cluster>` | 5434 to 5439 | Kubernetes |

## Notebooks

Papermill runs a notebook without opening it and saves the executed copy to `out/`. Two recipes
wrap it:

```bash
just nb pgmq_playground          # on its default server
just pgvector pg18               # the pgvector notebook against a chosen server
```

## The visualizations

```bash
just ingest                      # once: the SQLAlchemy docs, embedded
just app                         # the API on :8000
just viz                         # http://localhost:5173 (search) and /queue.html
```

Run locally, the scenes talk to the API, and every Run on the queue page starts real workers with
the chosen settings. The copies in this book replay recorded traces instead, which
`npm run save-traces` records and `npm run build:book` builds into the pages, both run in `viz/`.

The SQL consoles in the pgvector, graph, JSONB and pgmq chapters need no server, since they run
[PGlite](https://pglite.dev) in the page. `viz/src/sql/labs.ts` holds their seed data and examples.

## Building this book

```bash
just book                        # copy the executed notebooks, build the viz, render to book/_book
just book-preview                # live preview while editing
```

Pushing to `main` publishes the book to GitHub Pages.

## Further reading

[PGSimCity](https://github.com/NikolayS/pgsimcity) by Nikolay Samokhvalov simulates the internals of
Postgres 18 in the browser as a 3D city, from the stages of a statement to shared buffers, WAL,
checkpoints and autovacuum, and lets the reader trigger failures such as checkpoint storms or an
xmin horizon that stalls vacuum.
